correctness.rationale: The source method is instantiated with exactly matching implicit and delayed sigma. For every complex |z|>=1, Re(rho/sigma)>=0 is established by an exact unit-circle polynomial identity plus exterior harmonic minimum principle; sigma has all roots strictly within unit disk. Characteristic-matrix factorization and Perron–Frobenius domination by D^-1 B yield strict Schur stability whenever its spectral radius is below 1. The boundary has z=1 exactly, and above threshold a continuous family of nonnegative real matrices produces a real multiplier >1. The F_p witness follows from exact weighted-cycle entries, a cubic characteristic polynomial, and a strict all-p global minimum inequality. Standalone verifier passed 3 symbolic certificate families, 54 stable numerical instances, and 24 boundary/unstable cases. Finite tests are not treated as universal proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies numerical stability of every finite positive directed network under all admissible steps, lags and method parameters by one computable Perron-root threshold, rather than a mere sufficient bound. It supplies an exact necessity boundary and real unstable multiplier and exposes concrete noncommuting stable systems missed by every real-exponent version of the existing generalized numerical-range criterion. This is a structural numerical-analysis result with a reproducible stress-test, not a routine restatement of the known continuous-time M-matrix threshold. Scope and limitations are explicit.
